s.d: A person or thing supposed to bring bad luck.

foredoom to failure
x: This project is jinxed!

s.d: To cast a spell on.
To bring bad luck to.
To cause something to happen by mentioning it. Often used sarcastically.
x: “So you'll all be near New York!” Maggie says. “We don't know for sure yet.” Sara stresses. “Don't jinx it.”
I've no idea if she guessed what I was intending to do. I don't know why I was so reluctant to talk about it, even to her. Maybe I was afraid that verbalising my intentions would jinx it in some way.

s.d: To cause a bad outcome through verbal expression of certainty about a good situation or result. See knocking on wood, which is supposed to mitigate this effect.

x: Bart: I'm telling Mom and Dad! / Lisa: You're telling who? / Bart: Mom and Dad! / Girls: MOM AND DAD? JINX! / Janey Powell: Now you can't talk, 'til somebody says your name!

jird.e: Probably from Arabic جُرَذ (juraḏ, “a rat”) in a vulgar pronunciation.

s.d: gerbil of northern Africa

x: The jirds are treated with the suspension or solution obtained by this method. Only one jird is used for each compound for the primary screen.
Escherichia coli has been isolated from jirds that have died of septicemia.

jitney.e:
1886, originally for a five-cent US coin (a nickel); use for taxis and buses due to these services originally charging five cents as fare, popularized circa 1915.
The etymology is uncertain; it is believed to originate from Louisiana Creole jetnée, from French jeton (“token, coin-sized metal disc”), though this is disputed. Evidence for the Louisiana Creole French origin includes the geographic distribution (Southeastern US, especially Black/African-American), and early spelling as gitney, which

jitter.e: Possibly alteration of chitter (“to tremble, shiver”), from Middle English chittern (“to twitter, chatter”). Ultimately onomatopoeic; compare didder and teeter as well as German zittern.

a small irregular movement
(uncountable) A nervous action; a tic.

But Bolton deserve real credit, seeking to take advantage of their jitters at every opportunity in typically determined fashion.
